Answers in order-

Lower bore axis- the bore axis is the distance between the center of the bore (barrel) and the center of gravity (balance) of the pistol in your hand. The larger the bore axis, the more it will have a tendency of the barrel to tip up when firing. This is due to the longer leverage arm the bore axis provides, a lot like the difference between a short and long see-saws when they are side by side. The longer see-saw will move easier than the short one. In modern pistol design, you try to keep the barrel as close to the hand as possible to keep this "barrel flip" from happening.

Removable magazine- There is no removable magazine in a C96. The C96 holds 10 rounds in a fixed, internal box magazine located between the back of the barrel, and the triggerguard. That is the squared off portion that makes this pistol so distinctive, this is where the rounds are held. You reload the pistol via 10 round stripper clips- little pieces of folded metal that hold the ammunition by the rim. When reloading, the Mauser's slide will be locked in the rear position by the magazine's follower. There is a notch on top of the breech face that the bottom of the stripper clip will slide into. Then you use the middle part of your thumb to push all 10 rounds down into the magazine. When all the rounds are in the pistol, you pull the stripper clip out and the slide will close automatically, loading the first round and putting the gun into battery (ready to fire condition).

9x23 Largo- an obsolete cartridge (obsolete by means of there are more modern cartridges that deliver more power, speed, or heavier bullet per round, or that there just aren't very many pistols available that are chambered in it) that you won't be able to find at your local gun shop and will have to specially order it. Again, I'm not trying to diminish the 9x23 Largo as a caliber; a friend of mine has a Star pistol in 9x23 that's a blast to shoot. It just means there's very little demand for this cartridge anymore, mostly due to the overwhelming demand for 9mm Luger/Parabellum from shooters.

I hope this helps.
